title: Analytics dashboards, weekly reviews and cycle reviews with next-cycle generation
steps:
ANALYTICS ENGINE (PRD §10, §15; milestones M6). Pure, unit-tested domain functions in src/lib/domain/analytics (no I/O) + efficient SQL/repository queries (indexes from M3; EXPLAIN-check any new heavy query and record numbers in docs/performance.md):
- Strength: e1RM trends per exercise (from sets with reps+RPE; estimated values always labelled), weight/rep progression, PRs (rep-max PRs at each rep count, e1RM PRs, volume PRs) with dates, weekly volume (tonnage and hard sets), sets per muscle group per week (primary 1.0, secondary 0.5 weighting — documented), average RPE and actual-vs-target RPE deviation.
- Running: weekly mileage, distance trends, pace trends by run type (easy/tempo/intervals/long), long-run progression, race performances, frequency, optional HR.
- General: weekly sessions, total training time, adherence (planned vs completed vs skipped), session RPE (sRPE load = RPE × minutes), workload trends (acute:chronic ratio with clear caveats, monotony/strain), Muay Thai load, recovery notes.
- Trend vs noise: a documented statistical approach (e.g. rolling medians + minimum session counts + slope significance/effect size thresholds) that classifies changes as 'normal variation' vs 'real trend', used by reviews and the coach. Unit tests with synthetic series (flat noisy, steady improvement, decline, single outlier, sparse data).
- Expose them through services (and the M5 analytics tools must use these same functions — update the tools so the coach references the analytics).
- Integration tests on a seeded realistic dataset; performance: dashboard data for 2 years loads in < 150 ms server time (measure, record).

DASHBOARDS UI (Progress tab; PRD §10, §16; premium data viz — load the dataviz guidance by invoking the `dataviz` skill before building charts). Strength, Running and General views with an overview that makes 'am I improving?' obvious at a glance; every metric shown with context (period, comparison to previous period, what counts as good, estimated vs measured labels); exercise detail (e1RM trend, PR history, recent sessions), muscle-group volume vs target ranges, running mileage/pace charts, adherence and load charts. Charts: lightweight (prefer hand-built SVG or a tiny library; justify any dependency by bundle size), responsive at iPhone width, touch-friendly tooltips/scrubbing, dark-first palette consistent with the design tokens and discipline colours, accessible (text alternatives/tables, not colour-only, reduced-motion respected). Lazy-load chart code; route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip initial; no layout shift (reserve chart space; skeletons). Designed empty states for new users (week 1 has little data — explain what will appear and when). axe zero violations both themes. Playwright with seeded history: dashboards render the right numbers (assert against DB-computed values), exercise detail, period switching; screenshots of every view.

WEEKLY & CYCLE REVIEWS (PRD §11): 
- Weekly review generation (deterministic analytics + the coach for narrative/recommendations via the M5 agent, MockProvider in tests): planned vs completed, adherence, performance trends (normal variation vs real trend), actual vs target RPE, volume/intensity, running mileage/pace, Muay Thai load, recovery/fatigue signals, conflicting demands → recommended adjustments for next week as a PROPOSAL (M5 proposal lifecycle). Stored in the weekly_reviews table with the data snapshot used. A review screen (premium, scannable on iPhone) and a Today/Progress entry point when a week completes; owner can accept/modify/reject the proposed next-week adjustments; 'Generate next week' journey produces the next planned week as a new program version with rationale.
- Cycle review at block end: progress to primary goals, strength & endurance progression, accumulated fatigue, volume/intensity, exercise effectiveness (which lifts progressed), adherence, deload need → generates the NEXT CYCLE (exercises, loads from e1RM where available, sets/reps, intensity, running workouts, weekly schedule, progression strategy) via the M3 generator extended with progression from actual results (strength rules from PRD §5: consistently below target RPE → add load; above → reduce load/volume; missed reps accounted; declining performance → consider fatigue; multiple sessions before significant changes). Significant changes are explained; historical versions of programs and cycles are kept and viewable.
- Tests: integration (review computed from seeded weeks; next-week and next-cycle generation create new versions; history intact), scenario tests for progression rules, Playwright journeys: complete a seeded week → weekly review → accept adjustments → generate next week → see it in Train; end of block → cycle review → next cycle created; screenshots. Update docs (architecture analytics + reviews, performance numbers, milestones).
acceptance: Analytics are computed by pure, unit-tested domain functions: e1RM trends (estimated labelled), PRs, weekly volume and hard sets per muscle group, avg/deviation RPE, running mileage/pace/long-run progression, adherence, sRPE load and workload trends — with tests on synthetic series including noise vs real trend classification.
The coach's analytics tools use the same functions, and dashboard numbers shown in the UI match DB-computed values in Playwright assertions on a seeded dataset.

Progress dashboards (overview, strength, running, general, exercise detail) are premium, readable at iPhone width, show every metric with context and comparisons, have designed empty states for new users, and use accessible charts (text alternatives, not colour-only, reduced motion); axe zero violations in both themes.
Chart code is lazy-loaded; route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip; no layout shift; dashboard server time for 2 years of data measured (< 150 ms target) and recorded with EXPLAIN evidence for new heavy queries.

Weekly review: planned vs completed, adherence, trends vs normal variation, RPE deviation, volume/intensity, mileage/pace, Muay Thai load, fatigue and conflicts → next-week adjustments as a proposal the owner can accept/modify/reject; stored with its data snapshot.
Playwright: weekly review journey and 'generate next week' journey create a new program version with rationale visible in Train and history.

Cycle review at block end evaluates goal progress, progression, fatigue, exercise effectiveness, adherence and deload need, then generates the next cycle using progression rules from actual results (PRD §5 strength rules covered by scenario tests); significant changes are explained; previous programs/cycles remain viewable.
All gates pass locally (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf); docs updated; work committed on feat/m6-analytics-reviews with Conventional Commits.
